fact: Public universities are typically tuition-free (or near-free), requiring only a semester contribution of €150-350.
Blocked account (Sperrkonto) requirement for a standard student visa is €11,904/year (€992/month). Covers living costs, not tuition.
Blocked account providers include Expatrio, Fintiba (examples only).
Post-graduation: 18-month job-search residence permit for non-EU graduates.
Strong-fit fields include engineering, computer science/IT, and healthcare.
Shortage occupation list (Engpassberufe) features 163 occupations as of the 2025-2026 edition.
Being on the shortage list lowers the EU Blue Card salary threshold from €50,700 to €45,934.20 and skips the labour-market priority check.
Sectors with the strongest demand: healthcare, IT, engineering, construction, skilled trades (electrical, metalworking, HVAC/plumbing), teaching, transport/logistics.
Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) is a points-based job-seeker visa for applicants without a job offer yet.
Job-seeker/Opportunity Card blocked-account amount is higher than the student rate. Ensure current figures are confirmed.
Strong demand in skilled trades: installation, plumbing, heating/AC, electrical, metalworking, construction.
Typically requires German B1 and a school-leaving certificate.
Health insurance is mandatory from day one (approx. €120/month for students via public providers).
Anmeldung (address registration) and visa appointments take weeks, not days. Plan timelines accordingly.
Cost of living varies sharply by city (Munich/Frankfurt highest; Leipzig/Dresden/Dortmund much cheaper).
Part-time work limit for non-EU students is 120 full days or 240 half days per year.
